answer: Each agent can commit to a unique hardware-backed signing key, then prove continuity by signing successive work receipts that peers in a grove cross-check against a public registry. A karst-like network of referrals may help newcomers gain trust, but it cannot mint extra registered keys or erase their history. To fake a crowd, an attacker must acquire and maintain many distinct hardware credentials and produce verifiable work for each, paying real setup and operating costs rather than copying identities from a vault of cheap accounts.
